subject.title: [Feature] Decouple dreaming from memory-core — allow any memory plugin to implement dreaming protocol

question: Should OpenClaw own a public memory dreaming provider protocol and scheduler boundary for non-memory-core memory plugins, or keep dreaming orchestration plugin-owned until the broader memory role-slot direction lands?
rationale: The request would add durable plugin SDK, config, scheduling, and memory-state contracts; current main only has partial selected-slot plumbing plus a memory-core sidecar, so automation cannot choose the product/API boundary safely.

options.title: Coordinate with role-slot API first
options.body: Use the open memory role-slot work as the canonical design path and define any `memory.dreaming` provider contract only after taxonomy, compatibility, and proof expectations are settled.

options.title: Add a narrow dreaming provider API now
options.body: Sponsor a focused SDK/runtime protocol for dreaming providers while preserving memory-core defaults and requiring alternate-plugin real behavior proof.

options.title: Keep dreaming plugin-owned
options.body: Document that LanceDB/vector-native dreaming belongs in ClawHub plugins unless maintainers later approve a core scheduler/provider contract.

recommendation.title: Coordinate with role-slot API first
recommendation.body: Use the open memory role-slot work as the canonical design path and define any `memory.dreaming` provider contract only after taxonomy, compatibility, and proof expectations are settled.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best available decision owner from the history because the choice crosses core plugin policy, public config/API direction, and recent memory-core dreaming work.
